content.content:
Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm > 90, not >= 90, and it runs when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. ZOM-199 says >= 90 after the first 10 levels, but the code never changed from the original spec, so 90 exactly stays on tier 0.

Blake

content.content: {"result":"{\"id\": \"ZOM-42\", \"uuid\": null, \"identifier\": \"ZOM-42\", \"number\": 42, \"title\": \"Dynamic Difficulty\", \"description\": \"# **Part 1:**\\n\\nAllow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)\\n\\nWhat's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.\\n\\n* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n\\nWhat's not identical in the tiers:\\n\\n* Quantity of the items\\n* Quantity of the monsters\\n* Pre-warm period\\n\\nPlayers starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win streak:\\n\\n1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)\\n2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.\\n\\nPromotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.\\n2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player\\n3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this \\\"early exit\\\" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.\\n2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.\\n\\nPlease note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.\\n\\nThis also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.\\n\\nA losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.\\n\\n# **Part 2: Future expansion**\\n\\nIf a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:\\n\\nMonster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with\\n\\nPunk A | Punk B\\n\\nPunk B | Punk C\\n\\nPunk C | Punk D\\n\\nPunk D | Brute A\\n\\nBoss 1 | Boss 3\\n\\nBoss 2 | Boss 4\\n\\nBoss 10 | Boss 10\\n\\nIf the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.\\n\\nThe other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster \\\"rank\\\" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the \\\"next rank\\\" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:\\nPunk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C\\n\\nThen Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.\\n\\nThis will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. This will also prevent us from overcrowding the level with simply too many monsters.\", \"priority\": {\"value\": 1, \"name\": \"Urgent\"}, \"estimate\": null, \"url\": \"https://linear.app/harmonygames/issue/ZOM-42/dynamic-difficulty\", \"gitBranchName\": \"julialawson/zom-42-dynamic-difficulty\", \"createdAt\": \"2025-04-21T16:28:42Z\", \"updatedAt\": \"2025-05-31T02:54:30Z\", \"archivedAt\": null, \"completedAt\": \"2025-05-30T22:06:46Z\", \"startedAt\": \"2025-05-23T15:05:35Z\", \"canceledAt\": null, \"dueDate\": null, \"status\": \"Done\", \"statusType\": \"completed\", \"labels\": [\"Level Editor\", \"Backend Engineering\"], \"links\": [], \"attachments\": [], \"createdBy\": \"Robert\", \"createdById\": \"usr_Robert\", \"assignee\": \"arthur.blake@harmonygames.co\", \"assigneeId\": \"usr_cc3e90160f490686\", \"project\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"projectId\": \"dbab77c7-f871-4888-abf8-d98b52a41624\", \"team\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"teamId\": \"team_ZOM\", \"timeInStatusMinutes\": 177655, \"isArchived\": false, \"stateHistory\": []}"}

{"id": "ZOM-42", "uuid": null, "identifier": "ZOM-42", "number": 42, "title": "Dynamic Difficulty", "description": "# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Monster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with

Punk A | Punk B

Punk B | Punk C

Punk C | Punk D

Punk D | Brute A

Boss 1 | Boss 3

Boss 2 | Boss 4

Boss 10 | Boss 10

If the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.

The other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster "rank" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the "next rank" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:
Punk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C

Then Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.

values: How it works in the store builds today (iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133)
Each level has tier versions from -2 up; tier 0 is the default version of every level. A player plays the version matching their tier (or the closest one the level has).

Every new player starts on tier 0. Their starting tier is set when their 10th game ends (wins and losses both counted, not 10 levels cleared): if their average CPM over those 10 games is above 90 (cpm > 90) they move to tier 1, otherwise they stay on tier 0. Exactly 90 stays on tier 0.
The build, per Blake's reply to the store builds mail (ZOM-199 and the deck say >= 90 after the first 10 levels; the build was never changed from the original spec)

Tier -2 is an exception: you promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate up to the most recent 10 attempts of the player and promote if win rate is 80% or higher. This means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games (early exit). Every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted; this can trigger at any time, regardless of record. We also demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower (early exits possible, e.g. LLLWLL). With a win rate of 60 or 70% the player is neither promoted nor demoted. Every demotion resets the game record.

Yes. When a player is demoted, the level they are on also drops: their retry loads the next tier version down (each further demotion before a win drops it one more). The offset clears on their next win, and following levels load at the player's tier again (or the closest tier version the level has).
ZOM-303 (match3d#244), live in the store builds

A blunder (overfilling the match bar) enrages every monster on the board, including monsters still to spawn. Enrage adds walk speed and attack damage only; the HP boost from Blunder 2.0 is off. Values are per monster, below.
ZOM-254 trigger; ZOM-282 (replaces the ZOM-254 boost); per-monster values in the ZM monster enrage sheet
Enrage per monster (copied from the ZM monster enrage sheet, Live tab, as it stands Oct 1)

The baseline is in the ZM Difficulty folder: <https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AZoJzpzi48p9F6VTV0To9zdYPK8OZ5_IYWs8dKgVaRM/edit|ZM difficulty baseline register - Oct 6>. It has two tabs, Tickets and Rules in force. Robert and Brian can edit, Arthur can view, and you can comment.

**27 tickets made the list:**
• Live: 15
• Editor only: 8
• Replaced: 1
• Not shipped: 3

**Not shipped:** ZOM-202, ZOM-280, ZOM-293
**Editor only:** ZOM-162, ZOM-163, ZOM-173, ZOM-200, ZOM-201, ZOM-250, ZOM-277, ZOM-315
**Replaced:** ZOM-254 was replaced by ZOM-282. That's the only one: ZOM-282's closing note is the only one that says it replaces another ticket.

**When a new player gets their starting tier:** when their 10th game ends, with wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. If their average CPM over those 10 games is above 90 they go to tier 1. Everyone else stays on tier 0, including a player at exactly 90. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck say ">= 90 after the first 10 levels", but the build never changed from the original spec, so I put a comment on ZOM-199 saying what the build does.

What else I did on the tickets:
• Commented on ZOM-254 naming ZOM-282.
• Commented on each Editor only and Not shipped ticket that the change isn't in the store builds, with iOS 0.3.49 and Android 0.3.133 named.
• Left ZOM-42 and everything else untouched.

What's off the list:
• ZOM-258, the analytics/tutorial tickets you named (30, 49, 50, 161, 262, 275) and the duplicates.
• ZOM-312 and ZOM-295, which Blake marked "not tiers" on their PRs.

What's on without a title match: ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378, because Blake's closing notes on them start with "tiers:".

content.text:
I've built Leonard's baseline register, shared it with everyone on Monday's tuning invite, added the ticket comments his rules call for, and replied to him in the DM. [Here's my reply](https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/D05HB64NMQU/p1759302521000000?thread_ts=1759261706.530914&cid=D05HB64NMQU).

**The register:** [ZM difficulty baseline register - Oct 6](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AZoJzpzi48p9F6VTV0To9zdYPK8OZ5_IYWs8dKgVaRM/edit) is in the ZM Difficulty folder. It has the two tabs from the session agenda:
- **Tickets:** one row per ticket with Leonard's columns, plus the three Robert asked for in your group chat (assignee, done date in Pacific time, priority).
- **Rules in force:** starting tier, promotion, demotion, whether the level drops after a demotion, and enrage. The per-monster enrage numbers are copied as-is from the Live tab of your monster enrage sheet. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl are listed as "not copied yet", as the sheet has them.

**What's on it:** 27 tickets — 15 Live, 8 Editor only, 1 Replaced, 3 Not shipped.
- **Not shipped:** ZOM-202, 280, 293.
- **Editor only:** ZOM-162, 163, 173, 200, 201, 250, 277, 315.
- **Replaced:** ZOM-254, replaced by ZOM-282. It's the only one, because ZOM-282's closing note is the only one that says it replaces another ticket.
- **Added without a title match:** ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378, because Blake's closing notes on them start with "tiers:".
- **Left off:** ZOM-312 and ZOM-295, which Blake marked "not tiers" in his reviews on their PRs. Also left off are ZOM-258 and the analytics/tutorial tickets Leonard named, per his notes doc and DM follow-up, plus the two duplicates.

**Starting tier:** a new player gets it when their 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted. An average above 90 CPM puts them on tier 1, and exactly 90 stays on tier 0. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck say "90 or more after the first 10 levels", but Blake says the build never changed, so I went with the build. I commented on ZOM-199 saying what the build actually does.

**Ticket comments:** I added 13 comments, on ZOM-199, ZOM-254 and each Editor only and Not shipped ticket. The Editor only and Not shipped comments say the change isn't in the store builds and name iOS 0.3.49 and Android 0.3.133. I didn't create any new tickets and left ZOM-42 and the others alone.

**Where I followed later changes over the card text:** Leonard added things after writing the card, and I went with the newer instructions.
- **Sharing:** the card says only Robert edits, but a later checklist item gives Brian edit too. His notes doc says view-only for Arthur. Leonard gets comment access, as "everyone else" under the card's sharing rule.
- **Comments:** the card says to leave Editor only and Not shipped tickets alone, but the same checklist says to comment on them.
- **Attack power:** a card comment added it to the title keywords, which brought in ZOM-246, 250, 263, 277 and 315.
